guards: the population of declared `emit(env, {softFail:true, reason})` exit-code opt-outs does not grow without a deliberate re-baseline

poisonPill.why: `emit({ok:false})` sets a non-zero exit code since 2026-08-12 (plan §2b F4); before the coupling, 13 of 124 captured cross-skill invocations reported a failure in the envelope and still exited 0, which every caller that checks $? — shell scripts, CI steps, the pre-push hook — read as success. The runtime coupling is enforced at one seam and owned by tests/emit-exit-coupling.test.mjs. What NO runtime test can see is the population of declared opt-outs, because each one is individually legitimate: `{softFail:true, reason}` is real API for the cases where ok:false genuinely is not a process failure. An exemption mechanism nobody counts becomes the default, so this gate counts them and fails on GROWTH. The pill adds exactly one, in the shape a future author would write it, and the gate must exit 1 rather than absorbing it. It also fails on a REDUCTION, deliberately: a retired opt-out should be recorded in the baseline diff, not silently pocketed.
